subject: pathology
title: Intestinal pathology: malabsorption, IBD, polyps and Hirschsprung

steps.tx: **Coeliac disease** is a gluten sensitive enteropathy linked to HLA DQ2 and DQ8 where gliadin triggers immune injury in the small bowel. Testing uses **tTG IgA** with total IgA checked, and biopsy shows **villous atrophy** with crypt hyperplasia and intraepithelial lymphocytes. It causes iron deficiency, diarrhoea and failure to thrive, with itchy extensor vesicles of dermatitis herpetiformis in some patients. A **gluten free diet** heals the mucosa, while refractory disease carries enteropathy associated lymphoma risk that needs specialist care.
steps.say: Coeliac disease follows gluten exposure in genetically susceptible patients and flattens the small bowel villi severely. Serology and biopsy confirm the diagnosis, and iron deficiency often provides the first clinical clue for doctors. Strict gluten avoidance heals the mucosa, while refractory disease needs specialist care because lymphoma risk rises.

steps.tx: The biopsy shows a flat mucosal surface with **villous atrophy**, deep hyperplastic crypts and many lymphocytes inside the surface epithelium. The inset of tall normal villi makes the loss of absorptive surface easy to appreciate at low power. This triad is classic for **coeliac disease** and explains malabsorption with iron deficiency and diarrhoea in susceptible patients. In the exam, flat villi with crypt hyperplasia and **intraepithelial lymphocytosis** should immediately raise coeliac disease.
steps.say: This biopsy shows flat villi with deep crypts and many lymphocytes inside the surface lining of the bowel. The normal inset highlights how much absorptive surface has disappeared in the diseased mucosa shown here. That triad causes malabsorption and iron deficiency, and it should immediately suggest coeliac disease during examination revision.

steps.tx: **Crohn disease** can affect any part of the gut from mouth to anus with skip lesions, creeping fat, strictures and transmural inflammation. Noncaseating granulomas, cobblestoning and fistulas support Crohn disease, and smoking worsens its course over time in affected patients. **Ulcerative colitis** instead starts in the rectum and spreads continuously with mucosal inflammation, crypt abscesses and goblet cell depletion. Smoking protects against ulcerative colitis, colectomy cures its colonic disease, and **primary sclerosing cholangitis** associates strongly with it.
steps.say: Crohn disease affects any gut segment with skipped transmural inflammation, strictures and fistula formation over time. Ulcerative colitis starts in the rectum, spreads continuously and inflames only the mucosa in most patients. Smoking worsens Crohn disease but protects against ulcerative colitis, which colectomy can cure when medical therapy fails.

steps.tx: **Colorectal polyps** need sorting by malignant potential because hyperplastic polyps are usually benign while adenomas progress toward cancer. Tubular, tubulovillous and **villous adenomas** carry increasing risk, and larger size with high grade dysplasia raises that risk further. Sessile serrated lesions follow the BRAF pathway on the right side, while hamartomatous polyps mark syndromes such as Peutz Jeghers and Cowden disease. **Familial adenomatous polyposis** follows the APC pathway with hundreds of polyps, while **Lynch syndrome** follows mismatch repair failure with right sided cancers.
steps.say: Polyps need sorting because villous and large adenomas progress toward cancer far more often than small lesions. Hundreds of polyps suggest familial polyposis that needs prophylactic colectomy before cancer develops in young patients. Mismatch repair failure causes Lynch syndrome with right sided bowel cancers and tumours outside the bowel as well.

steps.tx: **Hirschsprung disease** follows failed neural crest migration that leaves the distal bowel aganglionic and unable to relax normally. RET mutations, Down syndrome association and male predominance support the diagnosis in a newborn with delayed meconium passage. Bilious vomiting and enterocolitis complicate the obstructed segment, while **suction biopsy** confirms absent ganglia with hypertrophic nerves and lost calretinin staining. Contrast enema shows a transition zone, and pull through surgery resects bowel up to the normally ganglionic segment.
steps.say: Hirschsprung disease leaves distal bowel without ganglia, so the segment cannot relax and obstructs from birth onward. Delayed meconium, bilious vomiting and enterocolitis support the diagnosis, while suction biopsy confirms absent ganglia definitively. Pull through surgery removes the abnormal segment and joins normally ganglionic bowel to complete treatment for most infants.
